reason: The mapping to Articles 10, 13, and 25(4) of the EU AI Act provides a defensible and sufficiently complete regulatory basis. Article 10 establishes the general obligation for high-risk AI systems to be trained on high-quality data, which implicitly supports the exclusion of non-relevant institutional data. Article 13 requires data governance measures, which can include opt-out mechanisms. Article 25(4) specifically mandates that users be provided with an option to opt out of the system's operation, which directly supports the control objective.
applicability_note: This control is applicable to third-party or cloud models, as these are the types of systems that would be subject to the EU AI Act's requirements for high-risk AI systems.
challenge_comment: The challenge is to ensure that the opt-out mechanism is enforceable and that the data governance measures are effectively implemented to prevent the use of institutional data without consent.
